originalTitle: Airline workers reportedly decline to help US agents as Trump migrant crackdown accelerates
summary: Expansion of immigration enforcement at US airports puts employees at odds with agents seeking 2,000 daily arrests
content: A dramatic increase in immigration enforcement at US airports has reportedly placed the airline industry at odds with the Trump administration as workers decline to help federal officials arrest their targets – many of whom have pending applications for visas, asylum or green cards. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) – both part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) – have expanded their collaboration to make as many as three dozen daily arrests at US airports last month, the Wall Street Journal reported. Some of the people who have been taken into federal immigration custody include a former au pair, an asylum seeker with sickle cell anemia who uses a wheelchair, and women who are married to US citizens and in the process of applying for lawful permanent residency, according to the New York Times. “It’s not people with criminal records,” said Ghassan Shamieh, a San Francisco-based immigration lawyer who had four clients detained at airports over 10 days. “You are talking about people with legitimate pending applications.” The latest crackdown represents another policy shift for the DHS, which has generally avoided immigration enforcement at airports so as not to disrupt domestic travel. But with a goal of 2,000 daily immigration arrests, ICE has started detaining people – many of whom have overstayed visas after coming to the US legally and have pending applications for immigration relief – in public places far from security checkpoints, whether at ticket counters or near gates. “This administration is working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport,” a DHS spokesperson told the New York Times. At one point, in Dallas, a federal agent went so far as to try to board a plane in search of a target. But the Southwest Airlines gate agent reportedly refused to allow the officer to do so without a warrant signed by a judge, and airline employees blocked ICE from seeing a computer screen while passengers were boarding. Southwest told the Wall Street Journal that it follows the law and has protocols “to ensure appropriate legal documentation is presented by law enforcement personnel before any information about customers is shared”. Still, hundreds of immigration arrests have already taken place at airports since the TSA and ICE began cooperating with one another last year. Members of the airline industry met with DHS in July to discuss their discomfort with the policy change. On top of the immigrants being detained, experts have raised concerns that the tense encounters could lead to escalation and unsafe conditions for bystanders or airline employees. “The actions that federal enforcement authorities have taken in our workplaces have raised glaring workplace, safety and legal concerns for flight attendants,” Sara Nelson, international president of the Association of Flight Attendants, wrote in a letter to carriers in March.

chineseSummary: 美国机场扩大移民执法，导致员工与特工人员产生分歧，寻求每天逮捕 2,000 人
chineseContent: 据报道，美国机场移民执法力度大幅加强，导致航空业与特朗普政府产生矛盾，因为工作人员拒绝帮助联邦官员逮捕他们的目标——其中许多人的签证、庇护或绿卡申请正在等待中。据《华尔街日报》报道，美国国土安全部 (DHS) 下属的移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 以及运输安全管理局 (TSA) 扩大了合作，上个月在美国机场每天逮捕多达三打人。据《纽约时报》报道，一些被联邦移民拘留的人包括一名前互惠生、一名患有镰状细胞性贫血且使用轮椅的寻求庇护者，以及与美国公民结婚并正在申请合法永久居留权的女性。旧金山移民律师加桑·沙米耶 (Ghassan Shamieh) 表示，“不是有犯罪记录的人。”他的四名客户在机场被拘留了十多天。 “你说的是那些有合法待决申请的人。”最新的打击行动代表了国土安全部的另一项政策转变，该国土安全部通常避免在机场实施移民执法，以免扰乱国内旅行。但为了实现每天逮捕 2,000 名移民的目标，ICE 已开始在远离安全检查站的公共场所（无论是在售票柜台还是在登机口附近）拘留人员，其中许多人在合法来到美国后签证过期，并且有待处理的移民救济申请。国土安全部发言人告诉《纽约时报》：“本届政府正在努力确保非法入境的外国人不能再飞行，除非他们离开我们的国家自行驱逐出境。”有一次，在达拉斯，一位
